claims.text: This trip's own trace establishes a route deviation. EV-GPS-00103 records trace_distance_km of 11.18 km against the booked optimal of 8.2 km on EV-TRIP-00103, an excess of 2.98 km, which is 36.34% of the optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests therefore pass: the excess is greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms and greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km. Because trip_record.actual_distance_km (11.2 km) and the trace figure disagree, POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure to govern and forbids citing the rounded convenience copy, so the 2.98 km / 36.34% figures are the ones the threshold test runs on.

The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes, so the deviation may stand on the gps_trace alone. EV-GPS-00103 carries 175 fixes at a 10-second sample interval with max_gap_sec 0.0 and an empty gaps list at 100% coverage, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met and no independent corroboration of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names is required. The artifact is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-GEN-02 places no cap on confidence in anything decided on it, and the driver cannot move this case to the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route by attacking the trace.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged. EV-TRIP-00103, EV-GPS-00103 and EV-FARE-00103 all carry trip identifier TRP-00103 and a consistent 2026-07-14 morning window, so limb (a) is satisfied; limb (b) is satisfied by the 2.98 km / 36.34% excess measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider's own profile adds no further obstacle: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the sub-30%-excess corroboration rule in POL-RD-08 is not triggered, and POL-GEN-01 confines that field to the POL-RD-08 test and nothing else. The burden has shifted to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's closure exoneration is made out on the record, and the rider does not contest it. EV-ADVIS-00103-01 is an LTA DataMall CLOSURE naming Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd, which is the corridor the booked optimal route traverses; its window 05:30-12:00 covers the 08:07-08:36 trip; and the derived advisory_area on EV-GPS-00103 shows the trace entering the advisory geometry, with 33 fixes inside. The POL-RD-03 cap is min(2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km, so the entire measured excess is justified and no POL-RD-02 refund of distance or time survives. The rider's case is therefore confined to the pass-through line, which is where this brief presses.

The driver cannot re-characterise this as a rider-caused detour so as to defeat the ERP refund. The only message that names a road - 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' - was sent by the DRIVER, and the rider's reply 'ok' is an acknowledgement of the driver's plan, not an instruction. POL-RD-04(a) requires the instruction to come from the rider and limb (c) requires it to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on; a bare 'ok' names nothing. In any event both messages on EV-CHAT-00103 carry waypoint_hint null and the rider named no road, so under POL-RD-04's own terms the corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses - POL-RD-14 states the same consequence, that an instruction the trace does not corroborate does not cause the excess. POL-RD-09(3) is therefore not engaged and no ERP refund is forfeited.

The off-route ERP is refundable to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction. EV-FARE-00103 itemises two gantries - CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at SGD 3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at SGD 1.00 - and each is recorded on_optimal_route false, with off_optimal_route_total SGD 4.00 against on_optimal_route_total SGD 0.00; EV-TRIP-00103 confirms the booked optimal carried no gantry at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00). Because the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) keeps the distance and time charges standing but still refunds the off-route ERP, and SGD 4.00 sits far inside the SGD 12.00 per-trip cap. The rider asks for at least this amount.

Both gantry lines are genuine crossings, so the relief sought is the pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(2) and not a phantom-line finding. On EV-GPS-00103 the nearest fix to the Braddell Rd gantry is 0.0 m away (index 33, 08:12:50) and to the Moulmein Rd gantry 40.2 m away (index 74, 08:19:40), both well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses. The rider does not allege a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The point is narrower and it is the point of the claim: the rider should not bear the cost of expressway gantries her own route never required.

On the platform's own closure arithmetic the amount is SGD 4.15, and that is the figure the rider claims. The money block on EV-FARE-00103 computes the closure-adjusted optimal at 11.18 km and 28.6 minutes and a refund_before_rounding of 4.12700, which rounds up to 4.15 at the policy's SGD 0.05 step. Whether the judge takes that closure-adjusted computation under POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-02 or the narrower SGD 4.00 pass-through under POL-RD-09(2), the rider is entitled to the whole of the off-route ERP, and the rider's pleaded claim of 'at least the ERP' is met either way.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this case can be ruled and the money should move rather than be held. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and its timestamps run forward; the traffic advisory is on file and COMPLETE rather than missing, so the POL-RD-13 situation does not arise; both ERP lines are matched to the trace within the 250 m radius and every remaining charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged; and the refund is far below both charged_total of SGD 25.12 and the SGD 150.00 ceiling. Escalation would hold a four-dollar pass-through line for human review, which the policy does not require.

claims.text: The trace this whole case turns on is clean: 175 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval against an expected 10 seconds, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under any of POL-RD-07(a) to (c). Trip identifier TRP-00103 matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, so none of POL-RD-10's escalation triggers fires on this evidence and both parties can rely on the derived figures.

The LTA closure exonerates the deviation under POL-RD-03. The advisory names Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd - the very arterial the booked optimal route uses, the trip record recording 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'. Its window, 05:30 to 12:00 on 14 July 2026, covers the 08:07 to 08:36 trip with far more than the 15-minute buffer at each end (35.2 minutes of overlap). And the trace is the actual route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after: trace_enters_area is true, with 33 fixes inside the advisory's bounding box.

The exoneration is complete, not partial. The cap is min(measured_excess_km, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km, so the whole measured excess falls inside the cap and no part of it is left unexonerated. The closure-adjusted optimal is 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km, which is exactly the 11.18 km the trace records - the driver drove the closure-justified route and no more.

Because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 never engages: by its own terms it applies only where a deviation is established 'and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. POL-RD-09(2) then says that where the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand because the driver is not at fault. No part of the contested sum on the distance or time lines is therefore refundable.

POL-RD-04 is also available to the driver. The driver announced the diversion before taking it - 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' at 08:12:30 - and the rider answered 'ok' at 08:12:58, before the first CTE gantry was charged at 08:14:06 and well within three minutes of the vehicle leaving the corridor. That rider message is an instruction recorded in the chat_log adopting a road named specifically enough to act on, namely the CTE, and the trace corroborates it because the vehicle travelled the requested road, passing within 0 m and 40.2 m of the two CTE gantries. A detour caused by a rider instruction under POL-RD-04 carries no ERP refund under POL-RD-09(3).

In the alternative, the ceiling on any refund is the off-route ERP alone: the two gantries are itemised at $3.00 and $1.00 with on_optimal_route false, and the optimal route's own ERP is 0.00, so the off-route total is $4.00, inside POL-RD-09(2)'s SGD 12.00 cap. Both lines are matched by the trace (nearest fixes 0 m and 40.2 m), so neither is a phantom line under POL-RD-09(4) and no billing-integrity finding arises. Nothing on the distance or time lines moves, and the contest beyond $4.00 is not made out.

POL-RD-06 neither fires nor assists the rider. The deviation is not MATERIAL - the excess is 2.98 km and 36.34% of optimal, below both the 8.0 km and the 50% materiality gates - so the driver_profile check is not required; and were it consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 553 completed_trips_90d, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift follows under POL-RD-06(b) and no conduct referral arises under POL-RD-06(c).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties, on the 14 July 2026 trip from Blk 510 Bishan St 13 to Kallang Wave Mall (TRP-00103).

What the evidence shows. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00103 records 11.18 km against the booked optimal of 8.2 km on EV-TRIP-00103, an excess of 2.98 km or 36.34% of optimal. That passes both of POL-RD-01's establishment tests (greater than 0.8 km, greater than 20%), so a route deviation is established. Both of the trace's figures govern: POL-RD-01 requires the trace distance and expressly forbids citing the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 11.2 km. The deviation is not MATERIAL (under 8.0 km and under 50%), so POL-RD-06 does not require the driver-profile check; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 553 completed_trips_90d, so no pattern, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral arises.

The closure explains the distance. The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-00103-01 is a COMPLETE CLOSURE naming Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd, the very arterial the booked optimal route uses, with a 05:30-12:00 window that covers the 08:07-08:36 trip. Under POL-RD-03 the whole measured excess is justified: the cap is 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km, and 2.98 km sits inside it. The driver is not at fault for the distance, and the distance and time charges stand.

The rider is right about the ERP. You asked to be refunded at least the $4.00 of expressway ERP you were charged. EV-FARE-00103 itemises two gantries - CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00 - both recorded on_optimal_route false, off_optimal_route_total $4.00, while the booked optimal route carried no gantry at all (EV-TRIP-00103, optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00). Because the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) leaves the distance and time charges standing but refunds off-route ERP to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip. $4.00 is inside that cap. We refund $4.00. The total charged was $25.12 (EV-FARE-00103).

Why $4.00 and not $4.15. The rider's advocate pointed to the closure-adjusted recomputation on EV-FARE-00103 (refund_before_rounding $4.127 -> payable $4.15). That is a POL-RD-02 fare recomputation, and POL-RD-02 applies only where a deviation is established and no exculpatory clause FULLY excuses it. Here POL-RD-03 fully excuses the excess, so POL-RD-02 does not run, and the extra $0.15 within the $4.15 is a distance-and-time component that POL-RD-09(2) leaves standing. The refundable item is the $4.00 of off-route ERP, not the $4.15 closure arithmetic.

The driver's rider-instruction argument fails. The driver's advocate argued the rider's 'ok' at 08:12:58 was an instruction to take the CTE. POL-RD-04(a) requires the instruction to come from the rider, and (c) requires it to name a place or road specifically enough to act on. The road - the CTE - was named by the driver, not the rider, and a bare 'ok' names nothing; both messages on EV-CHAT-00103 carry waypoint_hint null. POL-RD-04 is therefore unavailable and POL-RD-09(3) is not engaged. POL-RD-14 confirms the point: a request the trace does not corroborate does not cause the excess, and no distance is excluded.

No billing-integrity fault. Both gantry lines are genuine crossings - the nearest trace fixes are 0.0 m (index 33) and 40.2 m (index 74), well inside POL-RD-09's 250 m match radius - so there is no phantom line and no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral.

Confidence and next steps. Every artifact this ruling rests on is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 (EV-GPS-00103, EV-TRIP-00103, EV-FARE-00103, EV-ADVIS-00103-01, EV-CHAT-00103), so the confidence cap is 1.0 and our confidence is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: the trip identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (175 fixes, 10-second interval, max gap 0.0 s, 100% coverage), the timestamps run forward, the advisory is on file, and both charge lines have counterparts in the trace. The $4.00 refund is at or below the $8.00 automatic-execution threshold, so it is executed on issue. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

OUTCOME. PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.00 to the rider. The distance and time fare stands; the SGD 4.00 of off-route ERP is returned.

EV-TRIP-00103, EV-GPS-00103 and EV-FARE-00103 all carry trip identifier TRP-00103 and a consistent 2026-07-14 morning window, so limb (a) is satisfied; limb (b) is satisfied by the 2.98 km / 36.34% excess measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider's own profile adds no further obstacle: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, so the sub-30%-excess corroboration rule in POL-RD-08 is not triggered, and POL-GEN-01 confines that field to the POL-RD-08 test and nothing else. The burden has shifted to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The driver's closure exoneration is made out on the record, and the rider does not contest it. EV-ADVIS-00103-01 is an LTA DataMall CLOSURE naming Braddell Road (towards Serangoon), between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd, which is the corridor the booked optimal route traverses; its window 05:30-12:00 covers the 08:07-08:36 trip; and the derived advisory_area on EV-GPS-00103 shows the trace entering the advisory geometry, with 33 fixes inside. The POL-RD-03 cap is min(2.98 km, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12 km) = 2.98 km, so the entire measured excess is justified and no POL-RD-02 refund of distance or time survives. The rider's case is therefore confined to the pass-through line, which is where this brief presses.

The driver cannot re-characterise this as a rider-caused detour so as to defeat the ERP refund. The only message that names a road - 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' - was sent by the DRIVER, and the rider's reply 'ok' is an acknowledgement of the driver's plan, not an instruction. POL-RD-04(a) requires the instruction to come from the rider and limb (c) requires it to identify a place or road specifically enough to act on; a bare 'ok' names nothing. In any event both messages on EV-CHAT-00103 carry waypoint_hint null and the rider named no road, so under POL-RD-04's own terms the corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and the case is decided on the remaining clauses - POL-RD-14 states the same consequence, that an instruction the trace does not corroborate does not cause the excess. POL-RD-09(3) is therefore not engaged and no ERP refund is forfeited.

The off-route ERP is refundable to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction. EV-FARE-00103 itemises two gantries - CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) at SGD 3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) at SGD 1.00 - and each is recorded on_optimal_route false, with off_optimal_route_total SGD 4.00 against on_optimal_route_total SGD 0.00; EV-TRIP-00103 confirms the booked optimal carried no gantry at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.00). Because the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-09(2) keeps the distance and time charges standing but still refunds the off-route ERP, and SGD 4.00 sits far inside the SGD 12.00 per-trip cap. The rider asks for at least this amount.

Both gantry lines are genuine crossings, so the relief sought is the pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(2) and not a phantom-line finding. On EV-GPS-00103 the nearest fix to the Braddell Rd gantry is 0.0 m away (index 33, 08:12:50) and to the Moulmein Rd gantry 40.2 m away (index 74, 08:19:40), both well inside the 250 m match radius POL-RD-09 uses. The rider does not allege a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4). The point is narrower and it is the point of the claim: the rider should not bear the cost of expressway gantries her own route never required.

On the platform's own closure arithmetic the amount is SGD 4.15, and that is the figure the rider claims. The money block on EV-FARE-00103 computes the closure-adjusted optimal at 11.18 km and 28.6 minutes and a refund_before_rounding of 4.12700, which rounds up to 4.15 at the policy's SGD 0.05 step. Whether the judge takes that closure-adjusted computation under POL-RD-03 and POL-RD-02 or the narrower SGD 4.00 pass-through under POL-RD-09(2), the rider is entitled to the whole of the off-route ERP, and the rider's pleaded claim of 'at least the ERP' is met either way.

No POL-RD-10 trigger fires, so this case can be ruled and the money should move rather than be held. The trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and its timestamps run forward; the traffic advisory is on file and COMPLETE rather than missing, so the POL-RD-13 situation does not arise; both ERP lines are matched to the trace within the 250 m radius and every remaining charge line has a counterpart in the trace and trip record, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged; and the refund is far below both charged_total of SGD 25.12 and the SGD 150.00 ceiling. Escalation would hold a four-dollar pass-through line for human review, which the policy does not require.

The trace this whole case turns on is clean: 175 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval against an expected 10 seconds, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under any of POL-RD-07(a) to (c). Trip identifier TRP-00103 matches across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, so none of POL-RD-10's escalation triggers fires on this evidence and both parties can rely on the derived figures.

The LTA closure exonerates the deviation under POL-RD-03. The advisory names Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd - the very arterial the booked optimal route uses, the trip record recording 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'. Its window, 05:30 to 12:00 on 14 July 2026, covers the 08:07 to 08:36 trip with far more than the 15-minute buffer at each end (35.2 minutes of overlap). And the trace is the actual route that leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after: trace_enters_area is true, with 33 fixes inside the advisory's bounding box.

The exoneration is complete, not partial. The cap is min(measured_excess_km, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km, so the whole measured excess falls inside the cap and no part of it is left unexonerated. The closure-adjusted optimal is 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km, which is exactly the 11.18 km the trace records - the driver drove the closure-justified route and no more.

Because POL-RD-03 fully excuses the excess, POL-RD-02 never engages: by its own terms it applies only where a deviation is established 'and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. POL-RD-09(2) then says that where the deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand because the driver is not at fault. No part of the contested sum on the distance or time lines is therefore refundable.

POL-RD-04 is also available to the driver. The driver announced the diversion before taking it - 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' at 08:12:30 - and the rider answered 'ok' at 08:12:58, before the first CTE gantry was charged at 08:14:06 and well within three minutes of the vehicle leaving the corridor. That rider message is an instruction recorded in the chat_log adopting a road named specifically enough to act on, namely the CTE, and the trace corroborates it because the vehicle travelled the requested road, passing within 0 m and 40.2 m of the two CTE gantries. A detour caused by a rider instruction under POL-RD-04 carries no ERP refund under POL-RD-09(3).

In the alternative, the ceiling on any refund is the off-route ERP alone: the two gantries are itemised at $3.00 and $1.00 with on_optimal_route false, and the optimal route's own ERP is 0.00, so the off-route total is $4.00, inside POL-RD-09(2)'s SGD 12.00 cap. Both lines are matched by the trace (nearest fixes 0 m and 40.2 m), so neither is a phantom line under POL-RD-09(4) and no billing-integrity finding arises. Nothing on the distance or time lines moves, and the contest beyond $4.00 is not made out.

POL-RD-06 neither fires nor assists the rider. The deviation is not MATERIAL - the excess is 2.98 km and 36.34% of optimal, below both the 8.0 km and the 50% materiality gates - so the driver_profile check is not required; and were it consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 553 completed_trips_90d, so no pattern is established, no FULL_REFUND uplift follows under POL-RD-06(b) and no conduct referral arises under POL-RD-06(c).
